Commercial Clearance
1. UK Crown Copyright Expiration (CDPA 1988 s.163)
Under Section 163 of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, Crown Copyright in official British governmental, ministerial, and armed forces photography/artwork expires 50 years after the calendar year of publication. Official wartime records (1939–1945) reside in the worldwide Public Domain.
2. International Public Domain & Berne Convention
Primary sources, medieval illuminations, early modern treaties, and historic portraits published prior to 1928 or where the author died over 70 years ago reside in the Public Domain worldwide, permitting unrestricted commercial educational reproduction.
3. Open Access, OGL v3.0 & Creative Commons Deeds
Museum artifact photography and catalogued digital holdings are verified under Open Government Licence (OGL v3.0), Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY 4.0), or institutional public domain dedication deeds (CC0) with explicit accession shelfmark citations.
4. Double-Redundant Web Verification Architecture
Each record provides double redundancy: (a) direct clickable hyperlink to the repository's official main homepage, and (b) direct permalink to the catalogued artifact holding within the permanent digital collection.

Commercial Independence, Institutional Neutrality & Reprographic Certification

All curriculum publications, pupil anthologies, companion workbooks, and digital archives published under The History Revision Hub are independent commercial educational products engineered for nationwide and international institutional adoption. They maintain strict commercial neutrality and zero single-school attribution.

Audit Standard: ISO-compliant archival provenance concordance with verified shelfmarks and direct permanent collection hyperlinks.
Copyright Clearance: 100% verified under UK CDPA 1988, US Title 17, and the Berne Convention for unrestricted commercial educational deployment.
